title: LP2-15–16: derive the reported prime-distance digits
question: Does the reported 53-digit nearest-prime sequence follow word by word from the archived first-section rune transcription?
summary: The archived first section yields 57 word distances, not the reported 53. Their minimum edit distance is seven. The full 57-digit sequence still makes a palindrome on the first reverse-add; 53,845 of 100,000 fixed-multiset shuffles do likewise.

finding: The 53 reported digits do not match the 57 distances under the declared archived segmentation. A minimum of seven digit edits separates them. The 57-digit reverse-add result is nevertheless a palindrome because every mirrored digit pair sums to at most eight. In 100,000 matched digit-multiset shuffles, 53,845 results are palindromes.
limitations: The pasted source does not preserve the author's full transcription, exact separator choices or computation script. The figure gives one of multiple possible minimum alignments; it cannot identify which words the author omitted or changed. The archived text, though source-hashed, has not been reverified rune by rune against the image for this audit. The shuffle is conditional on a selected section and digit multiset. Human review pending.
next_steps: Verify disputed word breaks directly against page images and search for the original calculation, then define any cipher operation using the distance stream before treating it as a solving method.
